summary: Unexpected spike in 429 responses after overload protection rollout; client retry loop ignoring Retry-After (no jitter/backoff)
description:
Customer reports they began receiving frequent HTTP 429 responses starting 2026-01-21 after Redwood Hosted API overload protection rollout in us-east.

Issue summary
- Symptom: Increased 429s for /v1/chat/completions under bursty traffic, even when overall token usage is within normal daily range.
- Customer expectation: Prior behavior was mostly occasional 5xx/timeouts during spikes; customer assumed 429 indicates quota/rate limit misconfiguration.
- Current impact: Request failures increased; customer-side queue backlog grows due to retry loop.

Impact
- Customer-visible errors: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header present on many responses.
- Customer reports retries are "immediate" due to internal retry wrapper.

Environment
- Deployment: Hosted API
- Region: us-east
- Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions
- Model: redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct
- Traffic pattern: step-function bursts (batch jobs start top of hour)

Observed response details (from customer logs)
- Status: 429
- Headers: Retry-After: 2 (seconds) on most samples
- Body: Redwood overload-style error payload (customer pasted) indicating overload/load-shedding rather than account quota.

Customer questions
1) Do 429s mean we are being rate limited / billed / throttled due to quota?
2) What is the correct retry behavior?
3) Why did this change after rollout?

Initial hypothesis
- Likely overload-protection admission control returning deterministic 429s instead of downstream timeouts.
- Customer client may be retrying too aggressively, amplifying the burst (retry storm) and causing sustained shedding.

Requested from customer
- 10 minutes of raw request logs including timestamps (ms), request ids, and retry behavior (attempt count)
- Confirmation of retry settings (max retries, delay function, concurrency)
- Whether they are respecting Retry-After

Support note
- This ticket is customer-impacting and time-sensitive. Treat as Sev2 unless it escalates to sustained outage.
comments: 2026-01-22 09:14 PT — Dev Patel (Support) — Opened ticket from customer email. Acknowledged report and requested: (a) sample 429 responses incl. headers, (b) retry/backoff logic, (c) rough RPS + concurrency during bursts. Shared interim guidance: do not retry immediately; respect Retry-After; add exponential backoff with jitter.

2026-01-22 10:02 PT — BrightLedger (Customer) — Sent samples showing 429 with Retry-After: 2 and error message referencing overload protection. They confirmed their HTTP client retries up to 8 times with a fixed 100ms delay (no jitter) and retries are done in parallel workers. They believed 429 meant account throttling and increased worker count to compensate.

2026-01-22 10:20 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Clarified that 429 here is overload/admission control (not account quota), introduced to replace ambiguous 5xx/timeouts under overload. Confirmed Retry-After is authoritative and should be respected. Asked customer to confirm whether they also retry on streaming disconnects and whether they retry the same request idempotently.

2026-01-22 11:05 PT — Christine Wong (SRE) — Checked us-east gateway metrics for customer org id (shared in private). Noted correlation: bursts of retries with near-zero spacing cause shed rate to stay elevated for several minutes. Breaker state stays CLOSED; this appears to be edge admission control protecting downstream queues rather than a routing breaker OPEN event. No platform regression observed.

2026-01-22 11:18 PT — Dev Patel (Support) — Provided customer a recommended retry policy: max 3–5 retries; exponential backoff starting at 250–500ms; full jitter; cap at ~10s; respect Retry-After if present; do not increase concurrency in response to 429; implement a token-bucket on client side to smooth top-of-hour spikes. Also recommended to log attempt count and to avoid retrying streaming requests after partial output without app-level dedupe.

2026-01-22 12:03 PT — BrightLedger (Customer) — Implemented respect for Retry-After and reduced retries to max 4. Added random jitter (0–250ms) but still seeing some 429 spikes at the top of the hour.

2026-01-22 12:35 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Suggested switching to exponential backoff with full jitter (not small additive jitter) and adding a client-side concurrency limiter specifically for this route/model (e.g., max in-flight). Also recommended staggering batch job start times by 1–2 minutes and/or adding a local queue. Confirmed that overload 429s are not billed as successful inference and do not consume token usage, but requests still count toward general request metrics.

2026-01-23 09:10 PT — BrightLedger (Customer) — Updated retry implementation to exponential backoff with full jitter and max in-flight of 50. Reported 429 rate dropped from ~12% to <1% during bursts; p99 latency improved; no more runaway retry loops.

2026-01-23 09:30 PT — Christine Wong (SRE) — Verified in dashboards: shed rate for the org id returned to baseline during the same top-of-hour window; no abnormal breaker transitions. Recommended keeping these client settings and monitoring. No Redwood-side action required.

2026-01-24 08:45 PT — Owen Phillips (Support) — Closed as resolved. Summary: 429s were overload-protection admission control; customer retry loop (fixed 100ms, no jitter, high concurrency) amplified overload. Fix: honor Retry-After + exponential backoff with jitter + max in-flight. Shared link to official retry guidance and asked customer to reach out if they need help tuning for larger batch windows.
resolution: Resolved by customer: adjusted client retry/backoff behavior to respect Retry-After and added exponential backoff with full jitter plus in-flight concurrency limiting. No Redwood platform defect identified; overload protection behaved as designed (returning deterministic 429s instead of downstream timeouts).
customer_facing_follow_up: Sent customer the recommended retry policy and confirmed billing semantics (overload 429s not billed as successful inference). Provided links to overload error/retry guidance and asked customer to monitor top-of-hour batch behavior.
internal_notes: Pattern matches prior tickets: customers interpret 429 as quota and respond by increasing concurrency, creating a retry storm. Consider proactive comms/snippet in docs and SDK helper examples (TypeScript/Python/Go) highlighting full-jitter exponential backoff and honoring Retry-After. If recurring, add Console insight banner when sustained 429s with low spacing between retries is detected.
attachments: Customer log snippet (headers + response body) pasted in ticket comments; contains Retry-After and Redwood overload-style error payload.
